This PR addresses the remaining observability gap identified in #35808.

Currently, when a cache read fails, operators cannot distinguish between:
- **"Data not present"** (capacity eviction / cache miss)
- **"Data present but read failed"** (transfer error / corruption)

nodes.body: **[P2] Account timed-out prefetch tails.** can_terminate_prefetch() reports a timeout as a failed prefetch, then check_prefetch_progress() calls terminate_prefetch(), which sets operation.is_terminated(). In _page_transfer(), that stops later storage batches without setting prefetch_read_failed. A multi-batch timeout can therefore reach this block with completed_tokens < expected_tokens, but only l3_actual_read_tokens is incremented. The exported counters then satisfy l1l2_miss_tokens - l3_miss_tokens > l3_actual_read_tokens + l3_read_failed_tokens, so the missing tail is invisible even though the structured log says timeout. Please classify terminated/timeout separately and charge expected_tokens - completed_tokens to that outcome, with a deterministic test that terminates after the first batch.
Thank you for your reviewing. I have fixed this issue. I have separated the count of l3_read_failed_tokens from the prefetch_read_failed status.

inline_comments.body: **[P2] Account timed-out prefetch tails.** can_terminate_prefetch() reports a timeout as a failed prefetch, then check_prefetch_progress() calls terminate_prefetch(), which sets operation.is_terminated(). In _page_transfer(), that stops later storage batches without setting prefetch_read_failed. A multi-batch timeout can therefore reach this block with completed_tokens < expected_tokens, but only l3_actual_read_tokens is incremented. The exported counters then satisfy l1l2_miss_tokens - l3_miss_tokens > l3_actual_read_tokens + l3_read_failed_tokens, so the missing tail is invisible even though the structured log says timeout. Please classify terminated/timeout separately and charge expected_tokens - completed_tokens to that outcome, with a deterministic test that terminates after the first batch.
